title: Signatures of Topological Magnon Edge States in THz Spectroscopy and Cavity Response
authors: Ipsika Mohanty, Johannes Knolle, Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract: Topological magnon insulators (TMIs) have emerged as promising platforms for low-energy spin-based information processing, due to their non-trivial bulk magnon topology and robust, chiral edge modes that support dissipationless transport. Although theoretical models predict these edge states, direct experimental detection remains challenging due to their limited sensitivity to conventional probes. In this work, we propose an all-optical pathway to detect topological magnon edge modes in ferromagnetic TMIs. Our approach harnesses parametric amplification of edge magnons via resonant electromagnetic driving, enabled by magnetoelectric coupling mechanisms. We concentrate on two-dimensional van der Waals ferromagnetic materials on the honeycomb lattice with magnonic band gaps in the terahertz (THz) range. We show that a spin-dependent effective electric dipole moment, arising from dynamic charge fluctuations and consistent with the lattice symmetry up to next-nearest-neighbor interactions, gives rise to one-photon-two-magnon processes leading to parametric amplification. On this basis, we propose a THz pump-probe spectroscopy protocol in which edge modes are selectively amplified and subsequently detected in absorption. Furthermore, we discuss the possibility of using THz cavities, enabling selective coupling to edge modes while filtering out bulk contributions. These findings establish a route for probing topological magnets and open new avenues for experimental exploration of exotic topological phenomena in magnetic quantum materials.
summary: This paper outlines an advanced all-optical method to detect elusive topological magnon edge modes in 2D ferromagnetic insulators using THz spectroscopy. By leveraging the magnetoelectric coupling, they propose exciting these robust edge states through parametric amplification driven by resonant electromagnetic fields. This establishes a crucial experimental pathway for exploring topological phenomena in magnetic quantum materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop an all-optical method to experimentally detect robust, chiral topological magnon edge states in ferromagnetic Topological Magnon Insulators (TMIs), as conventional probes lack sufficient sensitivity.
main_result: The authors propose a THz pump-probe spectroscopy protocol that uses parametric amplification via magnetoelectric coupling ($\omega_{	ext{pump}} = 2\omega_{K,e}$) to selectively excite and detect these edge modes. They also discuss using THz cavities for spectral filtering of bulk contributions.
method: The theoretical framework combines spin wave theory (Holstein-Primakoff) with the inclusion of electromagnetic coupling ($\hat{H}_{	ext{int}}$), analyzing processes like magnon pair creation/annihilation under resonant driving conditions.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D van der Waals ferromagnetic material on a honeycomb lattice, modeled by an extended Heisenberg Hamiltonian incorporating Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). The detection relies on coupling the magnons to external THz electromagnetic fields.
key_observables: Topological magnon edge modes; spectral signatures in absorption following parametric amplification; two-magnon density of states ($ho^{(2)}(\omega)$); and bulk demagnetization effects.
important_parameters: Terahertz (THz) frequency range; pump intensity ($I$); resonance condition $\omega_{	ext{pump}} = 2\omega_{K,e}$; and the strength of magnetoelectric coupling.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the dipolar limit for the EM field ($\lambda \gg$ sample size), utilizes Linear Spin Wave Theory (LSWT), and employs approximations like the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate magnon band structures showing chiral edge modes, schematics of pump-probe setups using THz cavities, and plots detailing edge mode splitting versus pump intensity.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the theoretical necessity for an all-optical detection route to deriving the coupling Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{	ext{int}}$) via magnetoelectric effects. It then details two experimental proposals: THz pump-probe spectroscopy and cavity coupling, supported by symmetry analysis (AM conservation) when considering circular polarization.
why_interesting: This work bridges condensed matter magnetism with quantum optics/AMO physics by proposing a highly specific, non-linear optical measurement technique to probe exotic topological states in magnetic materials. The reliance on parametric amplification via magnetoelectric effects is key for AMO physicists studying light-matter interactions.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly addresses magnon dynamics in ferromagnetic insulators using THz spectroscopy and parametric amplification via magnetoelectric coupling ($\omega_{pump} = 2\omega_{K,e}$), which falls squarely into the realm of quantum-optics concepts applied to magnons/spin waves coupled to external electromagnetic fields.
